blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Running a British meeting is part choreography and part gentle facilitation. Your job is to keep things moving, make sure everyone is heard, and quietly stop the loudest voices from taking all the space — without ever being obvious about it.

A few techniques help. Start on time, always. Share the agenda beforehand. Invite the quietest person to speak early, before the room gets dominated. Use phrases like "thanks, that's really helpful — what do others think?" to move on without cutting anyone off. End with clear action items, owners and dates.

And, when possible, finish a minute or two early — it is almost always appreciated. A well-run British meeting leaves everyone feeling heard and, somehow, the work done. That is the craft.

items.q: According to the text, why should you invite the quietest person to speak early?
options: Because they usually have the best ideas
Before the room gets dominated by louder voices
So the meeting can finish on time
items.why: "Invite the quietest person to speak early, before the room gets dominated."

items.q: How should a well-run meeting end, according to the text?
options: With a summary email to everyone
With clear action items, owners and dates
With a vote on the agenda
items.why: "End with clear action items, owners and dates."

items.q: The phrase "thanks, that's really helpful — what do others think?" is used to…
options: praise the loudest voice in the room
move on without cutting anyone off
items.why: "Use phrases like… to move on without cutting anyone off."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Sharing the agenda in advance helps a meeting run well.
Everyone should feel heard by the end.
A good chair should openly silence people who talk too much.
items.why: Inferência: o texto insiste em conter as vozes altas "without ever being obvious about it" — silenciar abertamente contraria a ideia toda.

items.q: The final line "That is the craft" suggests that running a British meeting is…
options: a simple set of rules anyone can follow
something only senior managers can do
a skill that takes real judgement to do well
items.why: Inferência: chamar de "craft" (ofício) implica habilidade praticada, não uma receita simples.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Oliver preparando uma gerente júnior para conduzir sua primeira reunião britânica. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Right, so next week you're chairing your first cross-department meeting, and I want you to relax — you'll be fine. Let me give you a few things that have always worked for me.

First, start on time. Even if only half the room is there, begin. It sounds small, but people quickly learn that your meetings actually start when you say they will. And do send the agenda round the day before, not five minutes before.

Now, the tricky bit. You'll have one or two people who love the sound of their own voice, and you'll have someone quiet in the corner with the best idea in the room. Your job is to bring that quiet person in early — "Sarah, I'd love your view on this" — before the loud ones take over. When you need to move things along, thank the speaker warmly and turn to the others. Never just cut someone off; it lands badly here.

And please, close with actions. Who is doing what, and by when. Write it down, say it out loud, and if you can wrap up a couple of minutes early, everyone will quietly love you for it.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does Oliver advise about starting the meeting?
options: Start on time, even if only half the room is there
Start five minutes late to be polite
Start once the agenda is agreed
items.why: "First, start on time. Even if only half the room is there, begin."

items.q: When should the agenda be sent, according to Oliver?
options: At the start of the meeting
items.why: "do send the agenda round the day before, not five minutes before."

items.q: How should the junior manager handle a talkative person, according to Oliver?
options: Thank them warmly, then turn to others
Ask them to leave the room
items.why: "thank the speaker warmly and turn to the others. Never just cut someone off."

items.q: Why does Oliver want her to bring the quiet person in EARLY?
options: Because the agenda lists them first
To fill time at the start
Because quiet people leave meetings first
So that idea is heard before louder voices dominate
items.why: Inferência: ele diz que o quieto pode ter "the best idea in the room" e deve falar "before the loud ones take over".

items.q: What is Oliver's overall attitude toward the junior manager?
items.why: Inferência: ele a tranquiliza ("you'll be fine") e dá dicas concretas — tom encorajador e prático.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Chairing a meeting is part facilitation, part timing." Facilitation means…
options: making a process run smoothly for others
items.why: Facilitation = facilitação: ajudar o grupo a trabalhar bem, sem decidir por ele.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Every task got an ___ so we knew exactly who was responsible."
items.why: Owner = responsável, a pessoa encarregada da tarefa.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Let's write down the ___ before we leave, so nothing is forgotten."
items.why: Action items = itens de ação: as tarefas concretas combinadas na reunião.

items.q: "One director tends to dominate every discussion." To dominate means to…
options: control it and leave little room for others
items.why: To dominate = dominar: ocupar todo o espaço, sufocando os demais.

items.q: "Running meetings well is a real craft." Here, craft means…
items.why: Craft = ofício: habilidade que se aprende e aprimora com a prática.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs comuns em reuniões. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "She thanked him and gently moved on to the next point." To move on means to…
items.why: Move on = seguir em frente, passar ao próximo ponto.

items.q: "Never cut someone off mid-sentence — it lands badly." To cut someone off means to…
items.why: Cut off = interromper alguém antes que termine de falar.

items.q: "Let's go round the table so everyone has a say." This means to…
options: invite each person to speak in turn
items.why: Go round the table = dar a palavra a cada pessoa, uma de cada vez.

items.q: "Two managers pushed back on the new deadline." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "Once we agree the actions, let's make sure we follow through." This means to…
options: carry the plan out to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim aquilo que foi combinado.
